# Results — Study 614 (CLO Equity Yield — "the 15% Machine")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **"ECC and
OXLC pay ~15% distributions from CLO equity: the levered first-loss tranche of leveraged-loan
securitizations throws off enormous cash flows, and the funds hand them to you monthly — the
income is real"** — decomposed on the two listed CLO-equity closed-end funds **ECC** (Eagle
Point Credit, 2014→) and **OXLC** (Oxford Lane Capital, 2011→), against plain **HYG** (the
one-click credit alternative) and a **credit/equity-matched benchmark** (excess-on-excess,
Newey-West HAC). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `366d9cf7d356`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes, downloaded **twice**: auto-adjusted (**total-return**) and raw split-adjusted (**price-only**) — the monthly difference isolates the **distribution return**. OXLC's 2025-09 1-for-5 reverse split is handled on both legs |
| Tickers | ECC, OXLC (the two listed CLO-equity CEFs), HYG (high-yield credit, the one-click alternative), SPY (equity), BIL (1-3m T-bills, the cash proxy) |
| Window | ECC: 2014-11-30 → 2026-06-30 (**140 months**, 11.7 yrs); OXLC: 2011-02 → 2026-06 (**185 months**, 15.4 yrs) |
| Inference | Newey-West HAC *t* (6 lags; 3/12 as robustness) on the distribution component, the TR spread vs HYG, and the factor-model alpha; Sharpe races are **excess-vs-excess** over BIL |
| Execution / costs | passive buy-and-hold decomposition — entry at the first month-end close of each window (the one documented lag; there is no timing signal). Two one-way trades over 11.7 yrs at ~10 bps one-way ≈ **1.7 bps/yr** amortised; the funds' own drag (management + incentive fees + leverage interest, roughly 9-13%/yr of NAV per the funds' reports) is inside the tape |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** Unlike the mREIT study's REM, there is **no
> index fund for CLO equity** — the listed category essentially *is* ECC and OXLC, the two
> vehicles that scaled and made it to 2026. Funds that never scaled, delisted, or pivoted away
> from CLO equity are not on this tape, so the panel is survivor-tilted by construction: the
> honest reading is that these numbers describe the *best-case surviving wrappers*, and the
> category's full economics are, if anything, worse.

## The payout — the "15% machine" is real (it actually pays 17-19%)

Monthly **distribution component** = total-return minus price-only return, per fund
(HAC *t*, 6 lags):

| fund | window | distribution (bps/mo) | distribution (%/yr) | HAC *t* | TR CAGR | price-only CAGR | $100 → TR / price-only |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **ECC** | 2014-11 → 2026-06 (n=140) | **+133.30** | **+17.22%** | **+15.33** | **+1.75%** | **−13.46%** | **$122.5 / $18.5** |
| **OXLC** | 2011-02 → 2026-06 (n=185) | **+147.34** | **+19.19%** | **+15.35** | **+2.52%** | **−14.38%** | **$146.7 / $9.1** |

The advertised coupon is real — *bigger* than advertised: **+17.22%/yr** (ECC) and
**+19.19%/yr** (OXLC) of hard cash distributions, at HAC *t* ≈ **15.3** on both tapes. And the
erosion financing it is just as real: the price legs fell **−13.5%/yr** and **−14.4%/yr**.
$100 of OXLC *capital* became **$9.10** while the fund paid ~19%/yr of "income" the whole way
down.

## Risk & return — the funds vs their ingredients (ECC window, monthly TR)

| | CAGR | vol | Sharpe (excess over BIL) | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **ECC** | **+1.75%/yr** | 24.63% | **+0.14** | **−59.37%** |
| **OXLC** | **+0.64%/yr** | 32.29% | **+0.14** | **−61.08%** |
| HYG | +4.16%/yr | 7.21% | +0.34 | −15.25% |
| SPY | +13.78%/yr | 14.97% | +0.82 | −23.93% |
| BIL | +1.88%/yr | 0.57% | — | −0.16% |

Excess over bills, each fund on its own full window: ECC **+28.47 bps/mo at HAC
*t* = +0.43**, OXLC **+47.51 bps/mo at *t* = +0.81** — over a decade-plus, both 15%-machines
are statistically **indistinguishable from cash**, at 25-32% vol and −60% drawdowns. (OXLC's
CAGR in the table above is the joint ECC-window number; on its own 2011→ window it is
+2.52%/yr.)

## Headline test — total-return spread vs plain HYG (HAC *t*)

The one-click alternative: same income investor, same brokerage account, HYG instead of the
CLO fund. Both legs total return, each fund on its own full window:

| fund | spread (bps/mo) | spread (%/yr) | **HAC *t*** | fund TR CAGR | HYG TR CAGR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **ECC** (n=140) | **+7.87** | +0.95% | **+0.13** | +1.75% | +4.16% |
| **OXLC** (n=185) | **+17.78** | +2.15% | **+0.34** | +2.52% | +4.80% |

The 15-19% payer delivers a total-return surplus over the plain 5-6%-yielding credit ETF of
**zero, statistically** (*t* = 0.13 and 0.34) — while running **3-4× the volatility** and
**4× the drawdown**. On compounding, both funds finished *behind* HYG (the small positive mean
spreads are noise from the funds' violent 2020-21 swing).

## Alpha vs the credit/equity-matched benchmark

Newey-West (6 lags) regression of each fund's monthly **excess** return on HYG and SPY
**excess** returns — the passive levered-credit-plus-equity mix an investor could hold
instead. Full-sample betas (a benchmarking choice for a risk decomposition, stated openly):

| fund | alpha (bps/mo) | alpha (%/yr) | HAC *t* | β_HYG (t) | β_SPY (t) | R² | CAGR vs bench | maxDD vs bench |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **ECC** | −18.84 | −2.24% | −0.33 | +1.42 (+1.63) | +0.18 (+0.80) | 0.25 | +1.75% vs **+6.98%** | −59.4% vs −25.5% |
| **OXLC** | −33.55 | −3.95% | −0.66 | +1.24 (+2.81) | +0.41 (+2.59) | 0.24 | +2.52% vs **+10.60%** | −61.1% vs −28.2% |

No premium anywhere: the alphas are **negative and insignificant** (*t* = −0.33, −0.66 —
CLO-equity funds are so volatile that even a −2 to −4%/yr deficit doesn't clear a *t*-bar).
The passive copy of each fund's own betas compounded **5-8 pp/yr faster** with **less than
half the drawdown**. Note the R² of just 0.24-0.25: three quarters of the funds' variance is
idiosyncratic wrapper noise (premium/discount swings, leverage resets) you are paid nothing
to hold.

## Robustness — the zero spread / zero alpha is not a lag choice or a subperiod artefact

| variant | ECC spread *t* | ECC alpha *t* | OXLC spread *t* | OXLC alpha *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| NW lags = 3 | +0.14 | −0.36 | +0.36 | −0.67 |
| **NW lags = 6 (headline)** | **+0.13** | **−0.33** | **+0.34** | **−0.66** |
| NW lags = 12 | +0.13 | −0.30 | +0.33 | −0.65 |

Subperiods (joint ECC-window frame):

| window | fund | distribution | TR CAGR | price-only CAGR | spread vs HYG (*t*) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2016-01 → (ex the 2015 crunch entry, n=126) | ECC | +17.67%/yr (*t* = 14.9) | +2.44% | −13.19% | +6.53 bps/mo (+0.10) |
| | OXLC | +21.17%/yr (*t* = 14.0) | +3.06% | −15.25% | +30.75 bps/mo (+0.43) |
| 2020-07 → (post-COVID / high-rates, n=72) | ECC | +19.86%/yr (*t* = 11.1) | +7.98% | −10.23% | +38.29 bps/mo (+0.43) |
| | OXLC | +21.04%/yr (*t* = 9.7) | +5.30% | −13.25% | +32.98 bps/mo (+0.34) |

Even in the post-COVID "golden age of CLO equity" (floating-rate assets, rising short rates —
the sector's best-case regime), the payout hit ~20-21%/yr, the price legs *still* eroded
−10 to −13%/yr, and the surplus over plain HYG *still* rounds to statistical zero.

## Third axis — return OF capital, or return ON capital?

Pure returns arithmetic on the two full windows: the share of the annualised distribution
stream offset one-for-one by price erosion.

| fund | distribution paid | price leg | **share financed by price erosion** | kept (TR CAGR) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **ECC** | +17.22%/yr | −13.46%/yr | **78.1%** | +1.75%/yr |
| **OXLC** | +19.19%/yr | −14.38%/yr | **74.9%** | +2.52%/yr |

Roughly **three quarters of the "15% yield" is your own capital handed back** with a yield
label on it. What you actually *kept* — the total return — is 1.75-2.52%/yr: T-bill money.
This is measured on market prices; the funds' own 19(a) notices and NAV series (IPO NAVs
~$20 vs low-to-mid single digits today) tell the same story from the accounting side.

## Crisis autopsies — first-loss means first to fall

Peak-to-trough **total-return** drawdowns inside each fixed, documented window (daily tape):

| crisis | ECC | OXLC | HYG | SPY |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Credit crunch 2015-16 | −29.7% | **−57.1%** | −13.4% | −13.0% |
| Q4 2018 | −25.6% | −23.4% | −6.4% | −19.3% |
| COVID 2020 | **−66.1%** | **−73.8%** | −22.0% | −33.7% |
| Rate shock 2022 | −19.1% | −36.8% | −15.5% | −24.5% |

CLO equity is the **first-loss** tranche of a levered loan book, held inside a fund that
adds *its own* leverage on top. In every stress it fell 2-3× more than high yield and more
than equities — including −66% / −74% in eight weeks in 2020. The "income sleeve" is the
crash sleeve.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic factor world with a **planted** mean distribution stream and a **planted**
benchmark alpha (seed 614; payout jitter keeps the detector test non-degenerate):

| planted | distribution detector | alpha test | betas recovered |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| carry = 0, alpha = 0 (null) | +0.85 bps/mo (*t* = +0.33) | +33.40 bps/mo (*t* = +0.99) | 1.45 / 0.41 |
| carry = +120 bps/mo, alpha = −150 bps/mo | +120.85 bps/mo (*t* = +47.36) | −116.60 bps/mo (*t* = −3.44) | 1.45 / 0.41 (planted 1.60 / 0.45) |

Under the null neither detector manufactures significance; planted values light up.
*(A faithful-engine check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamps.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The "15% machine" *pays*: the distribution stream is **+17.22%/yr on ECC
  (HAC *t* = +15.33)** and **+19.19%/yr on OXLC (*t* = +15.35)** — bigger than advertised,
  and one of the most statistically solid cash streams on this desk. The erosion financing it
  is measured on the same tape (price legs **−13.46%** and **−14.38%/yr**). What does *not*
  exist is any surplus: the total-return spread vs plain HYG is **+0.13 / +0.34 HAC *t*** —
  zero. Survivorship: the two funds are the category's survivors (no index fund exists);
  named here.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Harvesting a 17-19%/yr coupon for 11.7-15.4 years left TR CAGR at
  **+1.75% / +2.52%/yr** (excess over bills *t* = +0.43 / +0.81 — cash, statistically) at
  25-32% vol and **−59% / −61%** drawdowns. No alpha vs a passive HYG+SPY mix (−2.2 / −4.0%/yr
  at *t* = −0.33 / −0.66) whose copy compounded 5-8 pp/yr faster at half the drawdown; a
  statistically zero spread vs one-click HYG at 3-4× the risk. The 9-13%/yr fee-and-leverage
  drag inside the wrapper is where the CLO cash flows went. Trading costs are irrelevant
  (~1.7 bps/yr); the wrapper is the mirage.
- **"Return OF capital or return ON capital?" — CONFIRMED (it is mostly return OF capital).**
  **78.1%** (ECC) and **74.9%** (OXLC) of the distribution stream was offset one-for-one by
  price erosion; $100 of capital became **$18.5 / $9.1**. Spend the distribution and you are
  spending your own principal — with a first-loss credit book and a −70% crisis profile
  attached.
